alignments.note: Conditional particle.
Indefinite pronoun rendered *any man*; rule 17's generic-noun clause heads on *any*, *man* being the supplied completion.

One Greek compound verb rendered by a whole English verb phrase; head on *teacheth*, the word realizing the compound's verbal head -διδασκαλεῖ, with *a different doctrine* its supplied completion. Heading on *doctrine* remains defensible, since it too glosses the διδασκαλ- element, but rule 91's test puts the head on the word answering to the lexeme's own head element.
Conjunction.
Finite verb rendered *consenteth*.
Ordinary negative to *not*.
Anarthrous dative; the case preposition *to* stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, discontinuously around the adjective under rule 15.
Attributive participle rendered by the bare adjective *sound* (ASV margin: Greek healthful).

Rule 105: the ASV's supplied appositional *even* is carried here by a substantival article (s009), and with that carrier it is its own `added` unit under rule 5; the article keeps only its own English words.
Substantival article standing after its noun and governing the following genitives; rule 22 gives it the supplied nominal *the words*, headed on the nominal word rather than on the determiner.
Article displaced by the possessive *our*, which belongs to ἡμῶν under rule 20.
Rule 20: the case preposition *of* stays with the noun, discontinuously around the possessive under rule 15.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *our*.
Name, split from Χριστοῦ under rule 26.
Name.
Conjunction.

Article preceding its head noun with a prepositional-phrase modifier the ASV recasts as a finite relative clause; rule 31 gives it the discontinuous *the … which* along with the case preposition *to* under rule 21, headed on *the*.
Head noun, left bare by rule 31 because its article precedes it.
Rule 31: a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the supplied copula, so *is* goes with the preposition, headed on *according*.
Noun.

review_notes: The supplied *even* is `added` because its appositive is carried by a substantival article, which rule 105 settles that way against the preposition carrier's fold.
τοῖς follows its noun and heads the appositional phrase, so rule 22 rather than rule 31's preceding-article clause governs it.
